abstract: In this paper, a robust 3D triangular mesh watermarking algorithm based on 3D segmentation is proposed. In this algorithm three classes of watermarking are combined. First, we segment the original image to many different regions. Then we mark every type of region with the corresponding algorithm based on their curvature value. The experiments show that our watermarking is robust against numerous attacks including RST transformations, smoothing, additive random noise, cropping, simplification and remeshing.
title: A new approach of 3D watermarking based on image segmentation
venue: international symposium on computers and communications

abstract: We studied an autoassociative neural network with dynamic synapses which include a facilitating mechanism. We have developed a general mean-field framework to study the relevance of the different parameters defining the dynamics of the synapses and their influence on the collective properties of the network. Depending on these parameters, the network shows different types of behaviour including a retrieval phase, an oscillatory regime, and a non-retrieval phase. In the oscillatory phase, the network activity continously jumps between the stored patterns. Compared with other activity-dependent mechanisms such as synaptic depression, synaptic facilitation enhances the network ability to switch among the stored patterns and, therefore, its adaptation to external stimuli. A detailed analysis of our system reflects an efficient-more rapid and with lesser errors-network access to the stored information with stronger facilitation. We also present a set of Monte Carlo simulations confirming our analytical results.
references: Dynamic Synapses in Neural Networks: A Review
Mean-Field Theory for Neural Network Dynamics
Monte Carlo Methods in Neural Network Analysis
title: Attractor neural networks with activity-dependent synapses: The role of synaptic facilitation

abstract: It is well-known that Sturmian sequences are the non ultimately periodic sequences that are balanced over a 2-letter alphabet. They are also characterized by their complexity: they have exactly (n+1) distinct factors of length n. A natural generalization of Sturmian sequences is the set of infinite episturmian sequences. These sequences are not necessarily balanced over a k-letter alphabet, nor are they necessarily aperiodic. In this paper, we characterize balanced episturmian sequences, periodic or not, and prove Fraenkel's conjecture for the special case of episturmian sequences. It appears that balanced episturmian sequences are all ultimately periodic and they can be classified in 3 families.
references: On the Complexity of Episturmian Sequences
title: A characterization of balanced episturmian sequences

abstract: One of the fundamental challenges of recognizing actions is accounting for the variability that arises when arbitrary cameras capture humans performing actions. In this paper, we explicitly identify three important sources of variability: (1) viewpoint, (2) execution rate, and (3) anthropometry of actors, and propose a model of human actions that allows us to investigate all three. Our hypothesis is that the variability associated with the execution of an action can be closely approximated by a linear combination of action bases in joint spatio-temporal space. We demonstrate that such a model bounds the rank of a matrix of image measurements and that this bound can be used to achieve recognition of actions based only on imaged data. A test employing principal angles between subspaces that is robust to statistical fluctuations in measurement data is presented to find the membership of an instance of an action. The algorithm is applied to recognize several actions, and promising results have been obtained.
references: Modeling Human Motion in Video Sequences
title: Exploring the space of a human action

abstract: Sturmian words are binary sequences of minimal complexity. We extend this notion to multi-dimensional sequences over grids and prove that balanced grid sequences correspond to mechanical words with irrational slopes in higher dimensions.
title: Balanced Sequences on Two-Dimensional Grids

abstract: Episturmian sequences generalize Sturmian words to arbitrary alphabets. We introduce a new morphic construction and show that all aperiodic episturmian words are generated by a unique directive sequence with bounded partial quotients.
title: Morphic Constructions of Aperiodic Episturmian Sequences

abstract: Fraenkel's conjecture remains open, but we prove it for the family of Thue-Morse-like sequences over three symbols. Our method uses overlap-free properties and a new substitution rule.
title: Fraenkel's Conjecture for Thue-Morse Variants

abstract: We define balanced sequences over finite fields and prove that they form a regular language. A pumping lemma for balanced languages is established.
title: Regularity of Balanced Sequences over Finite Fields

abstract: The complexity function p(n) = n+1 characterizes Sturmian sequences. We study sequences with p(n) = n+k for fixed k and show they are eventually periodic unless k=1.
title: Sequences with Linear Complexity n+k

abstract: We introduce the notion of balanced colorings of the integer lattice and prove a multidimensional analog of the three-distance theorem using discrepancy theory.
title: Balanced Colorings and the Three-Distance Theorem in Z^d

abstract: Using continued fractions, we construct a family of balanced sequences with exactly two periods and prove they are morphic but not automatic.
title: Morphic Balanced Sequences with Two Periods

abstract: We prove that every balanced sequence over 4 letters is ultimately periodic, providing a partial affirmative answer to a question by Erdős.
title: Balanced Sequences over Four Letters are Ultimately Periodic

abstract: The palindrome complexity of Sturmian words is known. We compute it for episturmian words and show it grows quadratically with a coefficient depending on the directive sequence.
title: Palindrome Complexity of Episturmian Sequences
venue: International Journal of Foundations of Computer Science

abstract: We define k-balanced sequences and prove that for k≥3, they must contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions of imbalances, contradicting uniform distribution.
title: Imbalance Progressions in k-Balanced Sequences

abstract: We present an efficient algorithm for constructing balanced sequences over 3 letters using continued fraction expansions. The method runs in O(n log n) and generates sequences with minimal imbalance.
title: Efficient Construction of Balanced Ternary Sequences

abstract: In this talk, we explore the connection between episturmian morphisms and Rauzy fractals. We show that the boundary of the fractal encodes the directive sequence.
title: Rauzy Fractals and Episturmian Directive Sequences

abstract: We introduce S-adic balanced sequences and prove that they are exactly the images of Sturmian sequences under finite substitutions.
title: S-adic Characterization of Balanced Sequences

abstract: We study the factor complexity of balanced circular sequences and show that they admit at most 2n+1 distinct factors of length n.
references: De Bruijn Graphs for Balanced Sequences
title: Factor Complexity of Balanced Circular Sequences

abstract: A new class of balanced sequences is constructed using the Wythoff array. We prove they are not morphic and have complexity 3n/2 + O(1).
title: Balanced Sequences from the Wythoff Array

abstract: This technical report surveys recent results on balanced sequences over non-integer alphabets and their applications in data compression.
title: Balanced Sequences in Data Compression: A Survey

abstract: We provide experimental evidence that balanced sequences over 4 letters exist and are not necessarily periodic, challenging existing conjectures.
title: Experimental Study of 4-Balanced Sequences

abstract: This extended abstract presents a new proof of Fraenkel's conjecture for sequences generated by the paperfolding morphism.
title: Fraenkel's Conjecture for Paperfolding Sequences

abstract: We explore the use of balanced sequences in DNA storage systems and show that Sturmian words achieve optimal redundancy.
title: Sturmian Sequences for DNA Data Storage

abstract: This working paper introduces the concept of quasi-balanced sequences and studies their growth rate and avoidance properties.
title: Quasi-Balanced Sequences and Avoidance
